"At least 72 Sudanese miners killed in air strike: Rights monitor"
BYLINE: "By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters" - AFP and Reuters attribution inside the body/byline. Photo credit AFP.

An air raid at a gold mine near the disputed Sudan-Egypt border killed AT LEAST 72 workers, per Sudanese rights group Emergency Lawyers (Khartoum-based), after survivors described chaos in the mountainous region.
Emergency Lawyers accused the EGYPTIAN MILITARY of carrying out the attack. On X on Sunday:
"Egyptian fighter jets targeted civilian miners in the northern Wadi area inside Sudanese territory, resulting, according to preliminary information, in the killing of 72 civilians."
ATTRIBUTION CAUTION: "The reported attack on Saturday cannot be independently verified, and Egypt has issued no official comment."

Second attack this year on the mountainous border region of Jabal al-Uqaydat, a gold mining area. Similar strikes, also reportedly carried out by Egypt, killed 23 workers at the site in JUNE.
The Egyptian military said at the time it had conducted a "large-scale operation" against illegal gold mining WITHIN ITS BORDERS. In June it said 223 people were detained, incl. 136 foreign nationals, and announced a campaign against "illegal gold mining and arms smuggling".
Emergency Lawyers said the attack occurred within Sudanese territory: "The repeated attacks on the gold and mineral-rich border regions reflect a desire by Egyptian authorities to expand and assert control over Sudan's natural resources."
The Sudan-Egypt border is disputed - both claim the resource-rich HALAIB TRIANGLE.
Images shared on social media and by local rights groups, which could not be verified, showed dozens of bodies in rubble and others wrapped in funeral shrouds.
CONTEXT: Since April 2023 the war between Sudan's army and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) has killed MORE THAN 200,000 people, pushing many into dangerous gold mining which fuels both sides' war efforts.
Egypt backs Sudan's army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan but considers the war at its 1,200km (745-mile) border from the Red Sea to Libya a significant security threat. Porous border is a conduit for gold, illicit trade and human trafficking; Egypt has used mass deportations.
